key_insight: Non-contact air-coupled ultrasound plus machine learning can rapidly predict cheese texture, revealing that plant-based cheeses match average firmness but not the full failure behavior of dairy cheese.
engineering_relevance: This offers a one-minute, non-destructive screening tool for formulation development and at-line quality control in cheese manufacturing.
method: Imaged 13 commercial cheeses (9 dairy, 4 plant-based) with 100 kHz through-transmission ultrasound.
Used two-channel C-scan features: amplitude and time-of-flight.
Trained a compact CNN to predict full true stress-strain loading/unloading curves from unseen slice images.
evidence_signal: The study analyzed 119 slices and 357 scans, and the model generalized across all 13 products without product-specific calibration.
watch_item: Performance may depend on product diversity and imaging conditions, so broader validation is needed before industrial deployment.
paper_title: Sounds Cheesy - Bridging the Texture Gap Between Dairy and Plant-Based cheese with Non-Contact Ultrasound and AI
